How to Liquidate & Cancel a UAE Freezone Company License Legally (Step-by-Step)

An exhaustive legal closure roadmap for foreign investors on Board Resolutions for Dissolution, visa cancellations, FTA tax deregistration, liquidator audit reports, bank closures, and official certificate of cancellation issuance.

15 Min Read · Updated July 2026
UAE Commercial Companies Law Dissolution Protocol
Liquidation Roadmap Essentials
1. Shareholder Resolution

Pass formal Board Resolution for dissolution and appoint an approved registered UAE liquidator.

2. Visa Cancellations

Cancel all employee, partner, investor residence visas, and Ministry of Interior Establishment Cards.

3. FTA Tax Deregistration

File final returns and obtain official VAT & Corporate Tax Deregistration Approval on EmaraTax.

4. Bank & License Deregistration

Close business bank account, submit audited liquidator report, and receive Certificate of Cancellation.

1. Why You Must Liquidate Legally (Dangers of Abandonment)

Abandoning a UAE company entity without executing formal legal liquidation is a critical error for international investors.

Under UAE Commercial Companies Law, simply letting a trade license expire without deregistration triggers cascading legal liabilities:

  • Compounding Renewal Fines: Freezone authorities accrue automatic monthly penalties ranging from AED 2,000 to AED 100,000+.
  • MoHRE Labor Blacklisting: License holders face MoHRE blacklisting, blocking shareholders from launching new UAE entities.
  • Immigration Travel Bans: Ministry of Interior (MoI) immigration holds prevent directors from entering the UAE.

3. Step-by-Step Freezone Company Liquidation Workflow

Executing formal legal dissolution follows a 6-step workflow:

  1. Step 1: Board Resolution & Liquidator Appointment: Draft and notarize a formal Board Resolution declaring intent to dissolve the company and appointing a registered auditor as Liquidator.
  2. Step 2: Visa Cancellations: Cancel all active investor, partner, and employee residence visas and cancel the MoI Establishment Card.
  3. Step 3: Clearances Collection: Obtain clearance certificates from landlord/flexi-desk provider, customs, telecom (e&/du), and utility providers.
  4. Step 4: FTA Tax Deregistration: Submit final VAT and Corporate Tax returns on EmaraTax and receive FTA Deregistration Approval.
  5. Step 5: Liquidator's Audit Report: Submit the final audited Statement of Account prepared by the appointed liquidator.
  6. Step 6: Cancellation Certificate: Pay final Freezone closing fees and receive the official Certificate of Cancellation.

4. FTA Corporate Tax & VAT Deregistration Rules

Under UAE federal tax laws, a business entity cannot complete trade license liquidation without first securing formal Tax Deregistration Approval from the Federal Tax Authority (FTA).

The company must file final VAT201 returns and Corporate Tax returns for the short tax period ending on the liquidation date, settle any outstanding tax liabilities or penalties, and obtain an official FTA Deregistration Certificate.

5. Corporate Bank Account Closure & Asset Distribution

Once all creditor claims are satisfied, the company's corporate bank account must be closed.

Remaining liquidation balances are transferred directly to shareholders' personal accounts according to their shareholding proportions, and an official Bank Account Closure Clearance Letter is issued for submission to the Freezone authority.
